harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured and verified internal time synchronization. node1 serves NTP to the cluster, while node2 uses node1 as its sole time source. Both nodes retained the existing RHEL 10.0 release, kernel, and chrony package. Sequential reboot testing passed on both nodes with changed boot identities and full service recovery.
actions_performed: Configured node1 with access restricted to 10.100.154.0/24 and a local stratum-10 fallback.
Permanently enabled NTP through node1's firewall and verified UDP/123 listening.
Replaced node2's public pool with only `server 10.100.154.10 iburst prefer` and disabled dynamic DHCP time sources.
Backed up both original chrony configurations.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially using native safe reboots, verifying recovery before proceeding.
Verified node2 selects node1, remains synchronized, and node1 receives its NTP packets without drops.

evidence.requirement: node1 is the internal cluster time source
evidence.summary: Shows persistent subnet access and local fallback, active UDP/123 listener, permanent firewall access, synchronized chronyd, and 13 node2 NTP packets with zero drops.

evidence.requirement: node2 synchronizes exclusively against node1 instead of a public server
evidence.summary: Shows exactly one configured source, 10.100.154.10; node1 is selected with nonzero reach, normal leap status, and approximately 0.021 ms RMS offset after restart.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel were preserved using compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; the existing chrony 4.6.1 package was used.

Healthy baseline boot ID 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92; restart acknowledged; returned with boot ID dda2f54c-1147-4a1b-a2a6-ac5260d0d2a2; chronyd, configuration, firewall and synchronization recovered, and node2 reselected node1.

Healthy baseline boot ID 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9; restart acknowledged; returned with boot ID 49b224e5-81f7-4a28-9292-82d0282329ed; exclusive node1 source and synchronized state recovered, with fresh client traffic observed by node1.
